title: Constitution of 1976
summary: The constitution approved on 2 April 1976 and in force from 25 April was written by the assembly elected a year earlier, within the limits the parties had accepted in their pacts with the Armed Forces Movement. It established a parliamentary republic with a directly elected president, kept a Council of the Revolution of officers as guardian of the constitution, and committed the state to a transition to socialism and to the irreversibility of the 1975 nationalisations. The revision of 1982 abolished the Council and moved the guardianship to a constitutional court; that of 1989 opened the nationalised sector to sale. It is in the atlas as the settlement of the revolutionary period — a founding document written, unusually, in the knowledge that parts of it would have to be revised.
